channel.title: Smart Cities Dive - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Smart Cities Dive (smartcitiesdive.com)

item.title: Libraries are central to community life. Many are in aging buildings that are falling apart.
item.description: Most U.S. library buildings face deferred maintenance, aging systems and limited funding options that put core civic services at risk, a new GAO report found.

item.title: Gaps persist between impact and opportunity in youth civic participation
item.description: Local government leaders saw K-12 schools as the most valuable institutions for positive effects on civic participation, according to a recent CivicPulse survey.

item.title: Will drivers accept technologies that limit speeding?
item.description: A study in California, where Gov. Gavin Newsom vetoed a bill to require speed-assistance systems in new vehicles, concluded that driver education and control would help acceptance.

item.title: Trump administration moves to require 100% domestic materials in EV chargers
item.description: Renewable energy advocates say the proposal would further delay the buildout of charging station infrastructure and undermine U.S. competitiveness.

item.title: FEMA shutdown threatens local reimbursements, training and long-term recovery
item.description: As Congress fails to reach a DHS funding deal, emergency managers are bracing for delayed payments, stalled grants and deeper uncertainty in an already strained federal disaster system.

item.title: NYC commits to $1B expansion of its automated traffic safety enforcement program
item.description: The New York City Department of Transportation will quadruple the number of red-light camera installations across the five boroughs and upgrade older equipment.

item.title: The missing layer in smart waste systems: resident engagement
item.description: Resident outreach and engagement technology is often treated as a communications add on. In reality, it functions as essential infrastructure.

item.title: Data centers pursue on-site power as state and local leaders worry about their impact on utility bills: report
item.description: State elections last year demonstrated “voter angst around inflation in utility bills,” according to the report's author. “We’d expect more of the same this year.”

item.title: California DOJ probes civil rights violations in Eaton Fire response
item.description: Investigators will examine whether evacuation delays in West Altadena, a historically Black community, reflect discrimination tied to race, age or disability.

item.title: Public sector interest in AI is high, but readiness is not, new research finds
item.description: Less than 2% of public sector leaders are deploying AI across departments as security concerns and lack of clear state and federal guidance hinder adoption, the survey found.
